Rashi on Eruvin 75a:10:1.hebrew: תנן חיצונה ולא פנימית שתיהן אסורות - הא עירבה נמי פנימית — תרוייהו שריין; אלמא, רגל המותרת לא אסרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:10:1.english: We learned: [If] the outer [courtyard established an eiruv] and not the inner, both are prohibited - [This implies that] if the inner [courtyard] also established an eiruv, both of them are permitted; evidently, a permitted foot does not prohibit.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:10:2.hebrew: אפילו רגל המותרת נמי - דקתני סיפא גבי עירבו שתיהן כל אחת לעצמה: ר"ע אוסר את החיצונה. ומשום לאשמועינן היא גופה — לא איצטריך, דמסיפא נפקא לן; דהשתא מותרת אסרה, אסורה מיבעיא:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:10:2.english: Even a permitted foot also - For it teaches in the latter clause [of the mishna] regarding [the case where] both of them established an eiruv, each one for itself: “Rabbi Akiva prohibits [carrying in] the outer [courtyard].” And [to say it was stated] in order to teach us this [case] itself — [it] was not necessary, since we derive it from the latter clause: for now [that even a] permitted [foot] prohibits, is [a] prohibited [foot] necessary [to state]?

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:11:1.hebrew: לעולם ר"ע - ולא תידוק מינה: עירבה — לא אסרה, אלא היא גופה קמ"ל, דרגל האסורה אוסרת. ודקא קשיא לך: מסיפא נפקא? אין ה"נ, אלא הא אשמועינן ברישא, והדר אמר: לא זו בלבד אסר ר"ע דהויא רגל האסורה, אלא אף זו — עירבה זו לעצמה וזו לעצמה, דפנימית רגל המותרת היא — אפ"ה רבי עקיבא אוסר החיצונה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:11:1.english: Actually, [it is] Rabbi Akiva - And do not infer from it: [If the inner courtyard] established an eiruv, it did not render [the outer courtyard] prohibited; rather, it teaches us this very [ruling]: that a prohibited foot renders [another courtyard] prohibited. And as for that which is difficult to you: [This] is derived from the latter clause! Indeed, so it is; rather, it teaches us this in the first clause, and then states: Not only this did Rabbi Akiva prohibit, which is a prohibited foot, but even that — [where] this [courtyard] established an eiruv for itself and that [courtyard] for itself, where the inner [courtyard] is a permitted foot — even so, Rabbi Akiva prohibits [carrying in] the outer [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:12:1.hebrew: טעמא דעירבה - פנימית, דהויא רגל המותרת:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:12:1.english: The reason is that it established an eiruv - [This refers to] the inner [courtyard], as it is a permitted foot:

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:12:2.hebrew: הא לא עירבה שתיהן אסורות - דרגל האסורה אוסרת. דהא ליכא למידק: הא לא עירבה, חיצונה המעורבת מותרת ושאינה מעורבת אסורה — דהא פשיטא דשאינה מעורבת אסורה, דהא כבר תני לה לעיל מתני'! ואי משום היא גופה — לאשמועינן רגל המותרת אינה אוסרת — לאשמועינן רגל האסורה, וליתני כגון: עירבה חיצונה ולא פנימית, חיצונה מותרת, וכל שכן האי! אלא ודאי, דוקא קתני:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:12:2.english: By inference, if they did not establish an eiruv, both are prohibited - That a prohibited foot renders [carrying in the other courtyard] prohibited. For one cannot deduce: “If it did not establish an eiruv, the outer [courtyard], which established an eiruv, is permitted, and the one that did not establish an eiruv is prohibited” — for it is obvious that the one that did not establish an eiruv is prohibited, as the Mishnah already taught this above! And if [you say that the clause was taught] for its own sake — to teach us that a permitted foot does not render [it] prohibited — let it teach us [this regarding] a prohibited foot, and let it teach, for example: If the outer [courtyard] established an eiruv and the inner [did] not, the outer is permitted, and all the more so this [case of a permitted foot]! Rather, it certainly taught [it] specifically.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:13:1.english: From the fact that the latter clause is Rabbi Akiva - For Rabbi Akiva disagrees on this matter.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:14:1.hebrew: שעשתה דקה - פנימית עשתה דלת קטנה לפני פתחה, וסילקה דריסת רגלה מחיצונה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:14:1.english: Where it made a dakkah - The inner [courtyard] made a small door in front of its entrance, and [thereby] removed its right of entry from the outer [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:14:2.hebrew: אין דריסת הרגל אוסרת - ואתרוייהו מילי דרבי עקיבא פליגי, ואפי' ארישא דקתני: "חיצונה ולא פנימית שתיהן אסורות". ונטרוה לרבי עקיבא עד דאסקיה למלתיה, והדר איפליגו עליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:14:2.english: The right of entry does not render [it] prohibited - And they disagree with both of Rabbi Akiva's statements, and even with the first clause, which teaches: "[If] the outer [made an eiruv] and not the inner, both are prohibited." And they waited for Rabbi Akiva until he concluded his statement, and then they disagreed with him:

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:16:1.hebrew: טעמא דשכח - אחד מן הפנימית, הא לא שכח — שתיהן מותרות. והא דלא כרבי עקיבא, דאי כר"ע, אי עירבו שתיהן נמי אסר על החיצונה. אלא לאו רבנן, ובשכח אסרי — אלמא רגל האסורה אוסרת:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:16:1.english: The reason is that [one] forgot - One [resident] of the inner [courtyard]; but if he did not forget, both [courtyards] are permitted. And this is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, for if [it were] in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, even if both of them made an eiruv, [the inner courtyard] would also prohibit the outer [courtyard]. Rather, is it not [the opinion of] the Rabbis, and when [one] forgot, they prohibit? Evidently, a prohibited foot renders [it] prohibited.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:1:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא שמה דירה - להא מילתא קמ"ל:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:1:1.english: I would have said [that] it is considered a residence - [It is] for this matter that [Rav] teaches us [this second ruling].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:1:2.hebrew: ה"ג ואי מהכא ה"א בתים לא ידענא כמה - כלומר, אי מהא ה"א: נהי דבחצירות שמעינן מינה דבתרתי סגי — מדנקט "צידו אחד עובד כוכבים", הא תרוייהו ישראלים שרי — אבל בתים, לא ידענא כמה לכל חצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:1:2.english: This is the reading: "And if from here, I would have said: Houses, I do not know how many" - That is to say, if [we derived it] from this, I would have said: Granted that regarding courtyards we learn from it that two suffice — since it stated, "its one side a gentile," which implies that [if] both of them are Israelites, it is permitted — but [regarding] houses, I would not know how many [are required] for each courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:20:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יהודה אמר רב חיצונה - דהתם, פנימית אסורה משום שכחה דחיצונה, דליכא למימר תסתלק מינה ותשמש, דליתיה לעירובה גבה. וחיצונה מיתסרא בשכחה דפנימית משום רגל האסורה. אבל נתנוה בפנימית — חיצונה הוא דמיתסרא בשכחה דפנימית משום רגל האסורה, אבל פנימית לא מיתסרא משום שכחה דחיצונה, דאחדא דשא ומשתמשא:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:20:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda said that Rav said: [In the] outer [courtyard] - For there, the inner [courtyard] is forbidden due to the forgetting of [a resident of] the outer [courtyard], as one cannot say, “Let it withdraw from it and make use [of its own courtyard],” for its eiruv is not with it. And the outer [courtyard] is forbidden due to the forgetting of [a resident of] the inner [courtyard] because of a forbidden foot. However, if they placed it in the inner [courtyard] — it is [only] the outer [courtyard] that is forbidden due to the forgetting of [a resident of] the inner [courtyard] because of a forbidden foot, but the inner [courtyard] is not forbidden due to the forgetting of [a resident of] the outer [courtyard], for it shuts [its] door and makes use [of its own courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:2:1.hebrew: אסור לעשות - לדור יחיד במקום נכרי, שלא ילמד ממעשיו. לפיכך, לא יערבו אלו עמו ולא ישתמשו עמו במבוי, כדי שיהא יחיד ויירא מן הנכרי שלא יהרגנו, ויצא:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:2:1.english: It is prohibited to do [so] - [That is,] to dwell [as] an individual in the place of a gentile, so that he does not learn from his deeds. Therefore, these [neighbors] may not make an eiruv with him, nor may they use the alleyway with him, so that he will be [left as] an individual [alone], and he will fear the gentile lest he kill him, and [so] he will leave.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:3:1.hebrew: דשמענא ליה לר' טבלא דאמר - בהא מילתא דרב:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:3:1.english: That I heard Rabbi Tavla say - [He said this] regarding this matter of Rav.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:3:2.hebrew: עובד כוכבים עובד כוכבים תרתי זמני ולא ידענא מאי קאמר - השתא ודאי מפרש למלתיה דרב: הוה מבוי שצידו אחד עובד כוכבים, אין מערבין אותו כולו, משום דאסור לעשות יחיד במקום עובד כוכבים. לשון אחר: חד למבוי, וחד לחצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:3:2.english: "A gentile, a gentile," two times, and I did not know what he was saying - Now, certainly, [Rabbi Tavla] was explaining Rav's statement: [his formulation] was, "An alleyway, one side of which is [occupied by] a gentile, they do not establish an eiruv for all of it, because it is forbidden to cause an individual [to dwell alone] in the place of a gentile." Another explanation: One [mention was] for an alleyway, and one was for a courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:4:1.hebrew: זו לפנים מזו - פנימית פתוחה לחיצונה, וחיצונה לרה"ר, ודריסת רגלה של פנימית על החיצונה לצאת לרשות הרבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:4:1.english: One within the other - The inner [courtyard] opens into the outer [courtyard], and the outer [opens] into the public domain, and the right of passage of the inner [courtyard] is through the outer [courtyard] to go out to the public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:4:2.english: [If] the inner [courtyard] established an eiruv - For itself, to carry in its courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:7:1.english: [If one] from the inner [courtyard forgot] and did not make an eiruv, both are prohibited - For the inner [courtyard] is a prohibited foot [i.e., a prohibited right of way].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:8:1.hebrew: נתנו עירובן במקום אחד - שעירבו שתיהן זו עם זו. והאי במקום אחד מפרש בגמ' שנתנוהו בחיצונה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:8:1.english: [If] they put their eiruv in one place - That both [courtyards] made an eiruv with each other. And this [phrase], “in one place,” is explained in the Gemara [to mean] that they placed it in the outer [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:8:2.hebrew: ושכח א' - אפי' מן החיצונה, ולא עירב — שתיהן אסורות; דפנימית נמי אסורה לטלטל בחצירה, משום דלא מציא למיחד דשא ואסתלוקי מחיצונה לאשתמושי באנפי נפשה, דהא ליתא לעירובה גבה, דאותו עירוב המתירן בחצירן הוליכוהו בחיצונה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:8:2.english: And one [person] forgot - Even [if one] from the outer [courtyard forgot] and did not contribute to the eiruv, both [courtyards] are prohibited. For the inner [courtyard] is also prohibited from carrying in its courtyard, because it cannot close the door and withdraw from the outer [courtyard] to use [its courtyard] on its own, since its eiruv is not with it — for that eiruv which permits them in their courtyard, they brought to the outer [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:8:3.hebrew: אם היו של יחידים - שאין בפנימית אלא אחד ובחיצונה אחד, אין צריכין לערב זה עם זה משום דריסת הרגל, דכיון דיחיד הוא, והפנימית הויא רגל המותרת ואינה אוסרת, וסתמא כרבנן. ואם היו שנים, אפילו בחיצונה — גזרינן דילמא אתי למישרי שנים בפנימית ואחד בחיצונה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:8:3.english: If they belonged to individuals - [Meaning] that there is only one [resident] in the inner [courtyard] and one in the outer [courtyard] — they do not need to establish an eiruv with each other on account of the right of passage. For since he is an individual, the inner [resident's right of passage] is a permitted foot and does not prohibit, and the anonymous [Mishnah] is in accordance with the Rabbis. And if there were two, even in the outer [courtyard], we decree lest one come to permit [a case where there are] two in the inner [courtyard] and one in the outer [courtyard].

Rashi on Eruvin 75a:9:1.hebrew: אף רגל האסורה אינה אוסרת - וממתני' מותבינן ליה לקמיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 75a:9:1.english: So too, the foot of one who is prohibited does not render [it] prohibited - And from the Mishnah we raise an objection against him below:

Tosafot on Eruvin 75a:15:1.hebrew: מתיב רב ביבי בר אביי - ק"ק, דה"ל לאקשויי מרישא מעיקרא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 75a:15:1.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye raised an objection - It is a bit difficult, for he should have raised the objection from the first clause initially.

Tosafot on Eruvin 75a:15:2.hebrew: אלמא רגל המותרת אינה אוסרת כו' - הא דלא מוקי בעשתה דקה, היינו משום דתיקשי: רישא וסיפא בעשתה דקה, ומציעתא — ההיא דשכח אחד מן הפנימית — בלא עשתה דקה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 75a:15:2.english: "Apparently, the foot of one who is permitted does not render it prohibited, etc." - The reason [the Gemara] does not establish [the ruling as referring to a case] where [the inner courtyard] constructed a partition is that it would be difficult: [Would] the first clause and the final clause [refer to where] it constructed a partition, and the middle clause — that [case] where one [resident] from the inner [courtyard] forgot [to establish an eiruv] — [refer to where] it did not construct a partition?

Tosafot on Eruvin 75a:1:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא דירת עובד כוכבים שמה דירה - אע"ג דאמר בריש פרקין דלכולי עלמא לא שמה דירה, הכא, דלהקל להתיר המבוי להחשיב כבתים וחצירות פתוחים לתוכו, אמר: שמה דירה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 75a:1:1.english: "I would have said that the residence of a gentile is considered a residence" - Even though it was stated at the beginning of our chapter that everyone agrees it is not considered a residence, here, where [it would serve] to be lenient, to permit the alleyway by considering [their dwellings] as houses and courtyards open into it, [the Gemara] said: "It is considered a residence."
